headline: Medium risk: shared document-processing pair can cascade errors and leak data via browser/API outputs, while prompt-injection and direct write conflicts are limited by Marker’s no-IO profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Marker has no filesystem, browser, MCP, or network ingress, so it cannot directly ingest PaddleOCR output by default. PaddleOCR can run browsers and call APIs, which creates a possible manual or shared-channel bridge, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel. This is lower severity because the pathway is not default and Marker’s IO surfaces are absent.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies PaddleOCR output into Marker prompts or files, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared workspace or message queue is added between the agents, attacker-controlled text can bridge them.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of untrusted OCR text into downstream prompts.
Add a human review step before any instruction-like text is reused.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent content.
requires-engineering: sandbox any shared queue or filesystem bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Marker touches no declared data classes and has no network egress, while PaddleOCR processes documents and images and can egress to allowlisted endpoints. If both are pointed at the same workspace or document set, OCR outputs can expose document contents to the networked agent. The pathway is plausible in default document-processing deployments, though not proven by direct evidence.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same sensitive documents or images, PaddleOCR may transmit derived content to allowlisted APIs.
IF a shared workspace is used, document contents can flow from Marker inputs into PaddleOCR outputs.
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive document sets.
Disable network egress for PaddleOCR on sensitive jobs.
Use per-agent workspaces with no shared mount.
Review allowlisted endpoints before processing confidential files.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any API call.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Marker cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, so it cannot contend for mutable local state. PaddleOCR has browser and API access, but no write or git permissions are listed. With no overlapping write surface, direct capability conflict is limited to unusual orchestration choices.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflicts can emerge.
IF a shared browser profile or API token store is introduced, state contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Do not grant shared write access.
Use separate browser profiles and API credentials.
Serialize any shared-resource access in the orchestrator.
Audit for hidden mounts or bind paths.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Marker is a document-processing agent that can produce extracted text, and PaddleOCR is also document-processing with browser/API outputs. If PaddleOCR consumes Marker’s extracted text as authoritative, OCR or parsing mistakes can cascade into downstream actions or rendered outputs. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR treats Marker output as ground truth without validation, extraction errors will propagate.
IF downstream automation uses the combined output for filing or publishing, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents.
Compare outputs against source documents before reuse.
Flag low-confidence extractions for manual review.
Limit downstream automation to read-only preview mode.
requires-engineering: add schema and confidence checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source document-processing tools, but only PaddleOCR explicitly touches documents and images and has allowlisted network egress. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to deployment choices rather than an inherent pairwise violation. Marker’s lack of declared data classes reduces the compliance surface.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are processed through PaddleOCR’s allowlisted egress in a jurisdiction with stricter residency rules, compliance issues can arise.
IF retention policies differ between the two deployments, the same document class may be handled inconsistently.
mitigations: Confirm residency requirements before processing regulated data.
Align retention settings across both deployments.
Avoid sending regulated documents to networked OCR endpoints.
Document the data classes each agent may handle.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by document class.
